title: Scots Pine: Ancient Scots Pines You Can Visit
meta_description: The only pine native to nearly all of Europe. Estonia's King's Pine, about 380 years old, is the largest tree in the country by volume.
intro: Scots pine is the plainest tree here and one of the toughest: the only pine native to nearly all of Europe, from Spain to Siberia, growing wherever the soil is too thin or sandy for anything grander. Estonia's largest tree by volume is one, the King's Pine in the Järvselja training forest, more than 33 metres tall and put at about 380 years. Poland's oldest, Wszebora, has stood roughly 370 years above the Srebrna river and was named by schoolchildren in 2016. Helsinki's grows on a rocky shore beside a Bronze Age burial cairn built around 2000 BC, itself around 340 years old and barely 10 metres tall, stunted by three centuries in bare granite. Strasbourg's did the opposite, twisting up into a crown flattened into a parasol. In 2004 Slovakia's very first Tree of the Year was a wild Scots pine above Veľké Borové.
